liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard to Handle** (2 reviews): The Hard to Handle performance is described as an absolute monster; The Hard to Handle performance is described as unbelievable [17][23]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The show starts with a great version of Bertha [23]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Cumberland Blues is characterized as bluegrass on acid [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-08-06.GEMS.Smith.Kaslow-Todd.109430.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 36 songs; 227 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1971-08-06.sbd.miller.96541.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1971-08-06.mtx.chappell.97015.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 163 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1971-08-06.mtx.seamons.96668.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 163 min; rated 3.62/5 by 8 [4]
- **gd71-08-06.aud.bertrando.yerys.129.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 135 min; rated 4.73/5 by 202 [9]. Said about its sound: Bertrando achieved a sweetspot sound using 1971 equipment, making audience noise a bonus; The tape sounds better than most 1980s audience recordings despite 1971 equipment; The sound is fantastic for an audience recording from 1971 [17][19][20][25]

## Around the show

- Bobby's 'Weather Report Suite' tease appears late in the Space Jam [15]
- The band played this show and the previous night at the Palladium [15]
- The Dead lived in nearby Watts and loved lighting up the L.A. sky [16]
- The reviewer notes it is a crime that no SBD exists for this show [19]
- The transition from The Other One into Me & My Uncle is magic [20]
- It was over 100 degrees in LA and inside the Palladium that day [22]
- After St. Stephen, Jerry, Bob, and Phil walked to their instruments [22]
- Bobby plays a short Weather Report tease after returning to The Other One [25]
- The first set is decent, but the second set is the main event [21]
- The two sources complement each other nicely, though both sound great on their own [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-08-06.GEMS.Smith.Kaslow-Todd.109430.flac24**: taped by Craig Todd and Harvey Kaslow; transferred by Jamie Waddell and Matt Smith; source: FOB Sony ECM-22P mics New Riders - MAR>R@ 7.5 ips.>DVD; GD - [1]. Also: The Hard to Handle from this AUD appears on the Fallout from the Phil Zone release [1]
- **gd1971-08-06.sbd.miller.96541.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [2]. Also: Master Reel supplies cover The Other One and a WRS Prelude tease [2]
- **gd1971-08-06.mtx.chappell.97015.flac16**: transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix of SBD(96541) and AUD (94261) with PATCH AUD(88816) [3]. Also: Fresh Apogee A/D transfers of Harvey Kaslow's AUDs were made by Matt Smith [3]
- **gd1971-08-06.mtx.seamons.96668.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [4]. Also: Charlie Miller transferred SBD to Master Reel, then CD, then FLAC using Samplitude; Harvey Kaslow's MAR was copied at 7.5 ips using a Revox A-77 [4]
- **gd71-08-06.aud.bertrando.yerys.129.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Ben Kasper; source: Audience - Sony ECM-22P's [9]. Also: Rob Bertrando, a pioneering taper, recorded this show at the Palladium [15]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-08-06 GD NRPS Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-08-06-gd-nrps-poster/) [28]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-08-06 GD NRPS Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-08-06-gd-nrps-poster-2/) [29]
- Fan art by auctions.yahoo.co.jp: [GRATEFUL DEAD AT THE HOLLYWOOD PALLADIUM・PAR... - Yahoo!オークション](https://auctions.yahoo.co.jp/jp/auction/k1074942774) [30]
